text:
maria: Quick heads-up — ran the KV fanout heatmap experiment for 16x4 (TP=2, PP=2) across 4 A100s. attaching notes shortly.

maria: Setup: model=gpt-24k, quant=q4_0, batch=8, seq=1024, thread=32. goal=reduce p99 and all-reduce overhead.

tao: Nice. Which metric are you focusing on first — throughput or tail latency?

maria: Primary: tokens/sec. Secondary: p99 latency and inter-gpu all-reduce traffic.

olivia: TLDR? Any regressions vs full-replication baseline?

maria: Heatmap: GPU1 holds ~42% of hot KV entries -> repeated fetches crossing PP boundaries. Fanout>1 amplifies fetches at step boundaries.

jamal: Can you paste the exact perf command you ran?

maria: `./run_serving_bench --model gpt24k --tp 2 --pp 2 --kv-shard policy=fanout,workers=4 --batch 8 --seq 1024 --threads 32`

maria: Profiling notes: nvprof traces show spikes in all-reduce around PP cut points. Overlap poor because kernel-selector fell back to a generic GEMM path after last selector change.

tao: That's the regression I suspected — kernel-selector fallback from PR #3245. @eng-bot showed increased allreduce BW in monitoring.

olivia: Can we force the optimized kernel and re-run to isolate selector vs sharding effects?

maria: Forced the optimized cuBLASLt-int8 kernel -> tokens/sec +12%, 99p latency -18ms. Network BW increased ~6% due to more frequent smaller all-reduces (metadata chatter).

jamal: So kernel fix helps compute but reveals comm pattern. We should try shard affinity to reduce cross-GPU fetches.

tao: Agree. Idea: prefer GPU-affinity placement that colocates KV owners with TP partners when feasible. Tradeoff: memory imbalance vs fewer fetches.

olivia: Do you have numbers for affinity run?

maria: Affinity policy results: max memory delta -9%, tokens/sec +9%, 99p -22ms. But hot GPUs had +8% peak allocs; eviction policy needed.

jamal: Another idea: hybrid partial-replication — replicate top-K hot keys across TP replicas and shard the remaining keys. That cuts fanout without full replication cost.

tao: Good. Add sweep: fanout in {1,2,4}, affinity on/off, replicate-topK in {0,1,5,10}. Capture tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, and all-reduce bytes.

olivia: I'll own the sweep and log aggregation. @maria drop nvprof traces and flamegraphs into PR.

maria: On it. Also note: kernel-selector change caused an ~8% regression in some shard configs — opening revert candidate / hotfix.

eng-bot: automated-check: referenced PR 4257, CI perf diff shows +7% tokens/sec (expected negative); please review. :eyes:

maria: Thanks — looping in runtime leads for rollout decision. Putting the hybrid replication + affinity sweep on the board. :raised_hands:
